newsitem.title: USA: Tricord shifts strategy after search fails.
newsitem.headline: Tricord shifts strategy after search fails.

text.p: Tricord Systems Inc said Wednesday its search for a strategic partner has been unsuccessful, requiring the company to change its business strategy and eliminate about 100 jobs.

"In September of 1996 the company engaged Smith Barney to assist in exploring various strategic alternatives, including the possibility of finding a strategic partner to strengthen the company's probability of success in the server market. That effort has not been successful," said chief executive John Mitcham.

The company said costs associated with bringing future server products through final development to market exceeds its available resources. "Therefore Tricord will not bring to market next generation servers," it said.

Instead, the company said, it will focus its resources on exploiting its unique distributed file system software technology and related expertise. The company said it is developing software and related hardware products for the Windows NT environment based on this technology.
"Tricord's strategy change will necessitate a reduction in the company's workforce, affecting approximately 100 employees," it said.
The company said it intends to manufacture and sell its Pentium-based Tricord PowerFrame Enterprise Server through 1997 and will honor warranty, service and support agreements.

The company also reported fourth-quarter revenues of $10.2 million and a net loss of $1.6 million after several special items. Revenues for the year-ago quarter were $15.5 million and the net loss was $5.1 million, also after special items.
